## Four levels, one path

Each lesson tells you its level, how long it takes and what you should know before starting. Follow the levels in order, or jump to what you need.

```{=html}
<div class="level-grid">
  <div class="level-card l1">
    <span class="num">Level 1</span>
    <h3>R foundations</h3>
    <p>Install R, learn the language, manipulate data with the tidyverse, write functions, import and clean data.</p>
    <a class="stretched" href="lessons/01-foundations/01-what-is-r.html" aria-label="Start Level 1"></a>
  </div>
  <div class="level-card l2">
    <span class="num">Level 2</span>
    <h3>Describe &amp; explore</h3>
    <p>Frequency tables, means and spreads, graphics with ggplot2, correlation — the language of data.</p>
    <a class="stretched" href="lessons/05-descriptive/21-frequency-tables.html" aria-label="Start Level 2"></a>
  </div>
  <div class="level-card l3">
    <span class="num">Level 3</span>
    <h3>Uncertainty &amp; inference</h3>
    <p>Probability by simulation, sampling distributions, bootstrap, confidence intervals and tests explained without magic.</p>
    <a class="stretched" href="lessons/07-probability/28-randomness-simulation.html" aria-label="Start Level 3"></a>
  </div>
  <div class="level-card l4">
    <span class="num">Level 4</span>
    <h3>Models &amp; learning</h3>
    <p>Linear and generalised linear models, tidymodels, trees and ensembles, PCA, clustering and an optional deep-learning track.</p>
    <a class="stretched" href="lessons/09-regression/38-simple-regression.html" aria-label="Start Level 4"></a>
  </div>
</div>
```

## How every lesson works

```{=html}
<div class="feature-grid">
  <div><div class="icon">🎯</div><h4>Clear objectives</h4><p>What you will be able to do at the end, stated up front.</p></div>
  <div><div class="icon">💡</div><h4>Intuition first</h4><p>Every idea starts from a concrete problem and a picture or simulation. The maths is there, in collapsible "Going deeper" boxes.</p></div>
  <div><div class="icon">🔎</div><h4>How to read the output</h4><p>Line-by-line guides to what R prints, so you can explain your results in words.</p></div>
  <div><div class="icon">⚠️</div><h4>Common pitfalls</h4><p>The misconceptions students (and researchers!) fall into, and how to avoid them.</p></div>
  <div><div class="icon">▶️</div><h4>Exercises in the browser</h4><p>Edit and run R code on the page — no installation needed — with hints and solutions.</p></div>
  <div><div class="icon">🧪</div><h4>Modern, reproducible R</h4><p>Native pipe, tidyverse, tidymodels, Quarto and project-based workflows.</p></div>
</div>
```

## Who is this for?

- **University students** in statistics, economics, biology, psychology, engineering and the social sciences who need R for their courses or thesis.
- **Self-learners** who want a structured path rather than scattered tutorials.
- **Instructors** looking for open material: the course can support a module of up to **9 ECTS / 72 hours**. All sources are on [GitHub](https://github.com/gianluca-sottile/An-R-Tutorial-for-Beginners).

No previous programming or statistics knowledge is assumed. If you can install software on your computer, you are ready.

::: {.callout-tip}
